name: manual_1c191f
claim: When a commit fails with 'stale lock file: index.lock' from a hygiene hook, do not just delete the locks. Git holds index.lock for the whole pre-commit run, so an existence-based scan flags the lock of the very operation it runs inside. Make the scan age-gated (locks younger than a few minutes belong to the current operation) and test both a fresh in-flight lock (ignored) and an old one (reported).

decisions.notes: orama-system#421, 2026-10-18: scan_stale_git_locks in scripts/review/repo_hygiene.py reported every lock under the git directory, so every commit through the hook failed. Reproduced across three real attempts, each with a fresh PID in the next-index lock name; no live git process held them afterwards, and deleting them as the message suggested changed nothing. Fix: STALE_LOCK_AGE_SECONDS = 300 plus a regression test; three older fixtures had to age their locks past the threshold. 62 of 62 hygiene tests pass. Until that PR merges other sessions may still hit it.
